subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discussion - Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Wong <sarah.wong@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discussion - Acme Health

Hi Sarah -

Thanks again for taking time today to walk through Acme Health's requirements. Wanted to put a short recap here so we have alignment on pain points, goals, and next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- Sporadic production slowdowns during morning/afternoon peaks when clinician workflows spike (~8-10am, 2-4pm PST).
- Need for strict data isolation and HIPAA-aligned controls (BAA, customer-owned keys, audit logs).
- Current vendor variability on latency and unpredictable throttling under load.

Primary goals:
- Dedicated GPU capacity (reserved) to guarantee predictable throughput during peak hours.
- Private network/VPC attachment and data isolation; logs retained for 365 days.
- SLA target: 99.9% uptime for inference service; p95 generation latency target of <= 350 ms for 512-token requests (clinically acceptable response window).
- Clear scaling plan to move from pilot -> pilot expansion -> full reservation within 90 days of pilot success.

Recommended Redwood config (initial proposal):
- Dedicated pool: 4x A100 80GB (dedicated to Acme account) with autoscale/burst to 6 GPUs for short peaks.
- Model variants: primary production model quantized to 4-bit to reduce latency/cost, with full-precision fallbacks for critical requests.
- Prefetch/KV cache for hot prefixes (clinical templates) to reduce repeated compute.
- Metrics: token throughput, 95/99 latency, error rate, and cost per 1M tokens.

Commercial notes:
- Estimated monthly commit (ballpark): $XXk–$YYk depending on final GPU count and commitment term. We can provide a formal quote once the SOW scope is locked.

Attachments: Acme_Dedicated_Capacity_SOW_draft.pdf (attached)

Next steps / owners:
- Marissa (me): share SOW draft and high-level pricing by EOD Fri (02/13).
- Sarah: confirm procurement contacts and any procurement cycles/PO requirements.
- Rishi: capture technical kickoff availability next week to run a short load/latency validation test.
- Both teams: review security questionnaire items Rishi will call out.

If that looks right, I’ll start the SOW and loop in our contracts/finance when you confirm procurement pace.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

Thanks Marissa, this looks good and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications: 

1) For the SLA and latency targets, can Redwood provide a short doc outlining how the 99.9% uptime is measured (per-region, per-cluster) and what exceptions exist for scheduled maintenance?
2) Regarding keys and BAA, procurement will need a high-level diagram of where customer-managed keys live and how audit logs are stored.

I'll confirm procurement contacts and timelines by EOD tomorrow. For initial procurement outreach, please include our procurement mailbox (procurement@acmehealth.com).

One note on burst: our compliance team prefers burst to be pre-approved and limited to short windows. We'll need to capture that in the SOW.

Thanks,
